title: thm:resolution is not a verbatim citable theorem; attribution vague, hypotheses tuned to conclusion

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** `thm:resolution`, "Attribution and status" paragraph; bibliography entries `\cite{Weinberger}`, `\cite{Lueck}`.

**The gap.** `thm:resolution` is attributed to "Connolly-Davis and Weinberger" but no precise theorem number or verbatim statement from any source is matched to the displayed statement. Faithfulness (state the cited theorem precisely, verify each hypothesis, show the conclusion gives the claim) is not met:

- The displayed hypotheses — contractible $X$ with proper cocompact $\Gamma$-action, finitely many orbit types, all isotropy finite of **periodic cohomology**, $d\ge5$, $\chi(\Gamma)\in\mathbb{Z}$, $\chi(\mathrm{Fix}(\bar t))=0$, plus obstruction vanishing — do not correspond to any single named theorem in the cited references that the critic can verify.
- In particular, the assertion that these **two scalar conditions** are *sufficient* (together with obstruction vanishing) to produce a **rationally acyclic** free $\Gamma$-resolution is not a statement one finds verbatim in Weinberger's *Topological Classification of Stratified Spaces* or in Lück's $\underline{E}\Gamma$ survey.

**Why it matters.** Importing a theorem is permitted only if it is stated precisely as published and its hypotheses are verified literally. A paraphrased, hypothesis-tuned "theorem" that bakes in the desired conclusion is not a legitimate citation; it hides the missing mathematics (see also the obstruction-vanishing gap).

**Fix.** Locate and quote a precise published theorem (with number) whose conclusion is the existence of the free $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic resolution, verify its hypotheses one-by-one for the witnesses, and confirm the conclusion is existence (not merely "obstruction vanishes").
